citations.narrative:
Four piglets under IACUC approved protocol (PO300) were presented for necropsy. The necropsy report findings suggest
regurgitation and aspiration as the cause of death for 3 of the 4 piglets. Veterinary observations determined that the
research staff primarily responsible for carrying out procedures under study protocol PO300 were inadequately trained to
work with the species to administer test material to piglets via oral gavage. Additionally, the IACUC noted that
inexperienced staff were responsible for performing procedures and monitoring the piglets without direct supervision of
the more experienced lab members as stated in the protocol. Inadequate staff training and study oversight can have a
significant impact on the health and welfare of research animals.
Prior to the inspection, the PI had proposed and the IACUC approved a corrective action plan that included re-training,
with veterinary oversight, of all research team members.
The research facility should ensure that all scientists, research technicians, and other personnel involved in animal care,
treatment, and use are qualified to perform their duties. This responsibility shall be fulfilled in part through the provision of
training and instruction to those personnel.
Correct by September 30, 2026

citations.narrative:
During the review of IACUC records, a reported incident involving the death of several piglets was found. On March 30,
2026, twenty-five piglets were born via cesarean section in accordance with an IACUC approved protocol (PO300). Within
1-2 days after the first procedure, six piglets died and five were humanely euthanized by the research staff. The laboratory
records indicate that the piglets’ health was deteriorating, however, the research staff continued to administer care on
their own instead of contacting the veterinary staff. Failure to notify the veterinary staff in a timely manner when health
concerns arise can result in pain, suffering, and/or death of the animals.
Research facilities shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include a mechanism of direct
and frequent communication so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-
being are conveyed to the veterinarian.
Prior to the inspection, the PI had proposed and the IACUC approved a corrective action plan with additional intensive
health monitoring, veterinary oversight, and specific study endpoints.
Corrected prior to the inspection on 06/15/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
AMY NOOYEN, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
